To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the organization of general motor activity is a critical factor in the expression of complex, goal-directed behavior.

(1) fetal rats exhibit intrinsic fluctuations in the level and variability in general motor activity, and (2) increased amplitude and variability preceding discrete presentations of an artificial nipple (a stimulus that elicits oral grasping) facilitates the expression of mouthing and oral-grasping responses to the nipple.
the organization of general motor activity in fetal rats influences the expression of mouthing and oral grasp behavior to an artificial nipple on Embryonic day 21.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ontogeny of the relation between general activity and the organization of specific behavioral responses in the developing rat.
the ontogeny of the neural systems controlling general activity and the development of specific behavioral responses.
how the expression of specific behaviors is influenced by the level and organization of general activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AN is an excellent model system to investigate the development of behavioral variability in the rat.
the expression of mouthing and oral-grasping behaviors is related to general behavioral organization, but that this relationship varies with the context of stimulation.
the expression of specific behavioral responses is dependent on the organization of general motor activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the organization of fetal activity is not a simple reflection of the level of arousal.
behavioral organization is not only a function of sensory stimulation but also a function of the intrinsic activity of the nervous system.
the expression of complex, well-defined behavior is facilitated when the level of general activity is increased, and the variability in the amplitude of general activity is high.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fetal activity is not simply a random fluctuation but a highly structured process.
fetal rats exhibit variability in general activity and that this variability may play an important role in the development of complex behaviors.
the expression of complex behaviors is not simply a function of the presence of the stimulus.
